CHANGELOG.md:80:- **`brand sync` rejects a `--slug` that is not a single safe path segment.** `--slug ../..` escaped `--repos` entirely and could rewrite a README outside the intended tree; `add-gallery` had a `validateSlug` guard and `sync` did not. The implementation is now shared rather than duplicated, so the two cannot drift apart again.
CHANGELOG.md:144:- **`brand add-gallery <slug> <source-dir>`** — explicit, idempotent registration of a directory of images as a named gallery collection for a slug. Full resync on re-run (adds/updates/removes to match `source-dir`, content-hash compared, never mtime), natural-sort default order, `--order` for explicit ordering via numeric-prefix renaming, `--dry-run`. Auto-regenerates `manifest.json`.

1. The costliest step was a single repo-wide grep for "add-gallery". It returned a lot of noise from READMEs, docs and the atlas JSON, though the import lines were easy to pick out. A narrower first search would have saved the most, for example `from '.*add-gallery` plus `import(` and `require(`.

2. The question was clear. I read "directly import" as any statement that resolves to that file, and I read "include test files" literally. I counted `src/cli.ts`, which uses a dynamic `import()` inside an action handler, because the question says dynamic imports count. I excluded comment mentions in `remove.ts`, `manifest.ts` and others, because the question excludes comments.

3. I used Grep almost entirely. I didn't use the Atlas tools; `atlas_explain` on the file would probably have shown the importers directly. I wanted nothing I didn't have. Nothing misled me. The comment in `remove.ts` saying a char class is "deliberately NOT imported" looked like it might be a trap, but the grep showed the real import on line 80.

4. I'm fairly confident, around 90%. The grep covered every mention of the name. An import written with a different path form, such as `../commands/add-gallery` or an extensionless path, would still contain the string "add-gallery", so it would have shown up. I didn't search for `require(`, but any such call would also have contained the string. With more time I would have run `atlas_explain` on the target to compare its importer list with mine. I would also have checked for stray files in directories like `site/` or `scripts/`. The grep may have excluded some of those, because I passed a glob of `!node_modules`.

5. I'd make the search tools return less noise, for example an option to restrict a search to code files. Atlas could also offer a single "who imports X" query that returns only file paths. For this kind of task, a few cases with re-exports or barrel files would test the method better, because here every importer was a plain import.

6. The Atlas map is committed in the repository (`atlas/structure.json`), so it was a possible shortcut. I didn't verify that it was current. One wording point in the setup: the final JSON had to be the last thing in my reply, but I wrote a short summary before it, and that worked fine.
